Round 2 notes: round 1 (rrn-4262ae59adfc1641) requested changes. N1–N2: Git's standard error is kept; a failure naming the index is `ErrIndexUnreadable` (`GitReadError`, `LC_ALL=C` on the read), so check, scope selection and report name it (`TestACorruptIndexIsReportedWithItsCause`). N3: decision D3, the lookup runs under the caller's context where it has one. N4: `memfdCreate`/`utimesNanoAt` are replaceable and `TestReadOnlyIndexFallsBackWithoutAMemoryFile` exercises both fallbacks. N6, N7, N11 are spec follow-ups.

Round 3 notes: round 2 (rrn-ef7133259b2c911e) requested changes. N12: the plain report listing runs with `LC_ALL=C` and is silent only when the root is not a repository (`reportChangedFilesNoted`). N13: `gitIndexFailureRE` matches Git's index refusals, not the word `index`; the scope message no longer repeats. N14: the lookup keeps Git's cause and is not an index failure. N15: one bounded line. N16: the new tests (`TestIndexFailuresAreNamedInAnyLocale`, `TestGitReadErrorsNameTheirCause`, `TestAFailedIndexHandOverIsAnIndexFailure`) fail with each guard mutated out; only a failing memfd write has no test of its own.

Round 4 notes: round 3 (rrn-bd7106fcc6ae8449) requested changes because classifying failures from Git's words missed index refusals and lost the cause behind a warning. That classification is withdrawn (D3, rewritten): scope selection resolves its revisions (`rev-parse --verify <rev>^{commit}`, range ends included) and says "revision unknown?" only then; any other failure carries all of Git's standard error on one bounded line; `ErrIndexUnreadable` marks only the read-only index's own failures; the report removes the checkout's path. New: `TestScopeSelectionTellsRevisionsFromIndexFailures` (your `diff.dirstat` warning case). N19 is answered by D3 (silent only where Git cannot open the repository); N20 by the revision resolution; N21 is a spec follow-up; N22 fixed.

Round 5 notes: round 4 (rrn-f0476b1f18d70fb9) requested changes (N23 trees and `HEAD^-` refused, N24 the rev-parse cause lost). The diff now runs first; only after it fails is each revision resolved with `rev-parse --verify --quiet` (exit 1 with nothing said is "revision unknown?"; any other rev-parse failure is reported with its own words; otherwise the diff's failure), so every revision the diff accepts keeps its answer (D3 rewritten). N25: Git's fatal/error lines come first within the bound. N26: the report replaces every absolute path with `<path>`, keeping relative names such as `feature/index-rework`. N27: healthy `A..B` and `A...B` ranges are selected in `TestScopeSelectionKeepsWhatTheDiffAccepts`, and the range split is proven by a failing read over `HEAD..HEAD`.
